c.tagline: Borneo's cat city — riverfront heritage and a gateway to orangutans and rainforest.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but Grab is far cheaper and more reliable; agree a fare first if taking a non-metered taxi.

emergency.note: 999 reaches police, ambulance and fire nationwide; 112 also works from mobile phones.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Padungan: Great Cat of Kuching statue, Padungan

hood_desc: The riverside promenade and colonial old town — Main Bazaar antiques, the Brooke-era courthouse, Chinese temples and the famous Cat Statue, with the Astana and Fort Margherita across the water; the sightseeing heart.
Kuching's Chinatown and café district along Jalan Padungan, lined with heritage shophouses, coffee shops, cocktail bars and the city's main nightlife; lively after dark.
A narrow heritage lane of Chinese temples, kopitiams, craft workshops and boutique guesthouses tucked behind the Main Bazaar; atmospheric, arty and walkable.
A local, riverside district famous for its big weekend market of jungle produce and Dayak crafts; down-to-earth and authentic away from the tourist core.
A modern residential and commercial zone around The Spring mall and Swinburne University, with malls and chain hotels; quieter and handy for shopping and day-trip departures.

water.note: Tap water is treated and better than most of Malaysia, but most people still boil or drink bottled.

transit.pay: Buses are paid in cash to the driver (about RM1-4); the Kuching hydrogen SmartBus loops the city centre. Small wooden sampan (tambang) river taxis cross the Sarawak River for around RM1.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am to 7pm; sampan river taxis run through the evening. After dark most travel is by Grab.
transit.note: Kuching has no rail transit. Getting around is by Grab, buses and the traditional sampan river taxis that ferry people across the Sarawak River between the Waterfront and the Astana/Fort Margherita side.

ferry: Pending Wharf (Express Bahagia boat to Sibu)

transit.m: Airport coupon taxi to city centre

tip.r: Tipping is not expected; a service charge is often already added at hotels and upscale restaurants.

food.desc: Springy egg noodles tossed dry in shallot oil and light seasoning, topped with char siu, minced pork and spring onion; Kuching's signature.

places.name: The Dyak

places.name: Top Spot Food Court

places.name: The Dyak

places.name: Zahayu Kek Lapis

places.name: Chong Choon Cafe

places.name: Top Spot Food Court

landmarks: Kuching Waterfront
A landscaped esplanade curves along the Sarawak River past colonial relics, sampan crossings and the golden sail of the Darul Hana bridge.
Semenggoh Wildlife Centre
Semi-wild orangutans swing in from the forest for morning and afternoon feedings at Borneo's most rewarding great-ape encounter, just outside Kuching.
Borneo Cultures Museum
Malaysia's largest museum, a striking golden-hulled landmark opened in 2022, unpacks Borneo's indigenous cultures across five immersive floors.
Fort Margherita and the Brooke Gallery
This whitewashed 1879 fort across the river tells the improbable saga of the White Rajahs who ruled Sarawak for a century.
The Astana
Rajah Charles Brooke's 1870 palace, built as a bridal gift, presides over manicured riverbanks as the Sarawak governor's residence.
Main Bazaar and Carpenter Street
Kuching's oldest streets pack antique shophouses, Chinese temples, kopitiams and craft dealers into the atmospheric heart of old Chinatown.
Tua Pek Kong Temple
Kuching's oldest Chinese temple, incense-wreathed since 1876, glows red and gold at a prominent corner facing the waterfront.
Cat Statues of Kuching
The Great Cat and its whimsical kin celebrate the city whose name sounds like the Malay word for cat, demanding a playful photo stop.
Sarawak State Museum
The oldest natural history museum in Borneo, founded in 1891 by Charles Brooke, displaying Iban and Orang Ulu artefacts alongside mounted wildlife specimens from across Sarawak.
Sarawak Textile Museum (Square Tower)
A restored 1879 riverside fort turned textile museum, showcasing Iban pua kumbu weavings, Malay songket and beadwork from Sarawak's many ethnic communities.

bus.note: Long-distance buses from Kuching Sentral run across Sarawak to Sibu, Miri and Sri Aman, and international coaches cross the border to Pontianak in Indonesian Kalimantan.

ferry.note: Express Bahagia passenger boats run down the coast and rivers from Pending Wharf to Sibu; small sampan river taxis cross the Sarawak River in town.

half.name: Semenggoh Nature Reserve
half.blurb: Semi-wild orangutans at twice-daily feedings, 30 minutes south of the city.

half.name: Sarawak Cultural Village & Damai
half.blurb: A living museum of Borneo's ethnic longhouses below Mount Santubong, near Damai beach.

full.name: Bako National Park
full.blurb: Rainforest trails, proboscis monkeys and sea-stack beaches reached by a short boat ride.

full.name: Annah Rais Longhouse
full.blurb: A traditional Bidayuh bamboo longhouse and hot springs in the hills southeast of Kuching.
